title: 2016 AMC 12B Problem 11
statement: How many squares whose sides are parallel to the axes and whose vertices have coordinates that are integers lie entirely within the region bounded by the line \(y=\pi x,\) the line \(y=-0.1,\) and the line \(x=5.1?\)

solutions.text:
A square whose left edge is \(x=k\) must fit below the lowest point of \(y=\pi x\) over its width, namely \(y=\pi k.\) For side length \(1,\) the possible left edges \(k=1,2,3,4\) contribute \(3+6+9+12=30\) squares. For side length \(2,\) the left edges \(k=1,2,3\) contribute \(2+5+8=15,\) and for side length \(3,\) the left edges \(k=1,2\) contribute \(1+4=5.\) A square of side at least \(4\) cannot fit, so the total is \(30+15+5=50.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The region sits below \(y=\pi x;\) note \(3\lt\pi\lt4,\) \(6\lt2\pi\lt7,\) and \(9\lt3\pi\lt10\)
In each vertical strip \(k\le x\le k+1,\) count the \(1\times1,\) \(2\times2,\) and \(3\times3\) squares that fit below the line, then add them up
